what: Nato summit begins with focus on defence spending as Zelenskyy and Trump due to meet - Europe live

clean_source_blocks.text: WASHINGTON -- US President Donald Trump will meet Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of this week's NATO summit in Ankara, the White House announced on July 5, as Washington seeks to revive stalled diplomacy over Russia's war while pressing Europe to take greater responsibility for the continent's defense. The announcement came a day after Trump held separate telephone conversations with Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin, underscoring the administration's effort to position itself as the key mediator in a conflict that has entered its fifth year with no breakthrough in peace efforts. Following the call, Zelenskyy said he had briefed Trump on the battlefield situation and that the two leaders agreed to continue discussions during the NATO summit.

Trump leaves Monday evening for the summit, and for days leading up to the trip has been airing grievances about how much the U.S. spends on defense compared with other countries. That's despite efforts from Mark Rutte, the alliance's secretary-general, who tried to feed the ego of the tempestuous U.S. leader in an Oval Office meeting last month. There, he displayed large charts on easels showing what he called " The Trump Trillion " — how much allies had boosted their spending commitments since 2017. Luke Coffey, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute, a conservative think thank in Washington, described the Ankara gathering as the "first report card" after last year's summit in The Hague.

"There is a real prospect to put an end to this war, and America's resolve is decisive," Zelenskyy wrote on X. Zelenskyy also warned that intelligence suggests Russia is preparing yet another massive air campaign against Ukraine, following the deadly barrage on the night of July 1–2. "This is in the spirit of Putin -- right after America's Independence Day and before the NATO summit in Ankara. Russia wants to add to the evil and kill people," Zelenskyy said in his video statement on July 5. The Kremlin said Trump's roughly 90-minute conversation with Putin included Trump's reiteration of his readiness to continue mediation efforts, while Putin repeated Moscow's position that any settlement must take account of Russia's "fundamental approach" to resolving the conflict.

The speed with which most NATO countries have tried to heed Trump's call to spend 5% of their annual gross domestic product on defense over the next decade underscores how the U.S. president has reshaped the alliance and bent it to his will — even as he continues to spar with its members over the Iran war, his flirtation with annexing Greenland, and various personal tiffs. "President Trump fully expects that all allies will step up immediately and get on the path to 5% and do it with urgency," Matt Whitaker, the U.S. ambassador to NATO, told reporters in a preview of the administration's message before this week's summit in Ankara.

WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump got what he wanted from NATO at last year's summit: an alliance whose members had largely acceded to his demands to step up their defense spending.

This week when he meets leaders in Turkey, his mission is to enforce that pledge.

The speed with which most NATO countries have tried to heed Trump's call to spend 5% of their annual gross domestic product on defense over the next decade underscores how the U.S. president has reshaped the alliance and bent it to his will — even as he continues to spar with its members over the Iran war, his flirtation with annexing Greenland, and various personal tiffs.

"President Trump fully expects that all allies will step up immediately and get on the path to 5% and do it with urgency," Matt Whitaker, the U.S. ambassador to NATO, told reporters in a preview of the administration's message before this week's summit in Ankara.

Trump leaves Monday evening for the summit, and for days leading up to the trip has been airing grievances about how much the U.S. spends on defense compared with other countries. That's despite efforts from Mark Rutte, the alliance's secretary-general, who tried to feed the ego of the tempestuous U.S. leader in an Oval Office meeting last month. There, he displayed large charts on easels showing what he called " The Trump Trillion " — how much allies had boosted their spending commitments since 2017.

Luke Coffey, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute, a conservative think thank in Washington, described the Ankara gathering as the "first report card" after last year's summit in The Hague.

"If NATO members play their cards right — if the leaders show up demonstrating a commitment and a reasonable plan to meet these spending targets — then it'll allow President Trump to take a victory lap," Coffey said.

---

[Lähde: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]
WASHINGTON -- US President Donald Trump will meet Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of this week's NATO summit in Ankara, the White House announced on July 5, as Washington seeks to revive stalled diplomacy over Russia's war while pressing Europe to take greater responsibility for the continent's defense.

The announcement came a day after Trump held separate telephone conversations with Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin, underscoring the administration's effort to position itself as the key mediator in a conflict that has entered its fifth year with no breakthrough in peace efforts.

Following the call, Zelenskyy said he had briefed Trump on the battlefield situation and that the two leaders agreed to continue discussions during the NATO summit.

"There is a real prospect to put an end to this war, and America's resolve is decisive," Zelenskyy wrote on X.

Zelenskyy also warned that intelligence suggests Russia is preparing yet another massive air campaign against Ukraine, following the deadly barrage on the night of July 1–2.

"This is in the spirit of Putin -- right after America's Independence Day and before the NATO summit in Ankara. Russia wants to add to the evil and kill people," Zelenskyy said in his video statement on July 5.

The Kremlin said Trump's roughly 90-minute conversation with Putin included Trump's reiteration of his readiness to continue mediation efforts, while Putin repeated Moscow's position that any settlement must take account of Russia's "fundamental approach" to resolving the conflict.

The calls come as months of US-led diplomacy have failed to narrow the gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Russia continues to insist on control of the occupied parts of Ukraine's east, while Kyiv has rejected territorial concessions.

White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly confirmed that Trump would meet Zelenskyy on July 8.

---

[Lähde: Daily Sabah]
The timetable for the July 6-8 NATO summit in Ankara was confirmed. The 36th edition of the event is a highly anticipated occasion for members of the military alliance, which appears to be falling out with the top contributor, the United States. President Donald Trump is among the most prominent guests of the event, while host President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan is expected to showcase Türkiye’s influence in the changing global order.

The summit will be inaugurated by NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte with a news conference ahead of bilateral talks and main sessions. Rutte will speak to journalists at the International Media Center set up at the Presidential Complex at 3:45 p.m. local time on Monday.

payload.title: Trump ja Zelenskyi tapaavat Naton huippukokouksen yhteydessä Ankarassa
payload.summary: Naton huippukokous Ankarassa alkaa tilanteessa, jossa Yhdysvallat painostaa liittolaisiaan kasvattamaan puolustusmenoja ja pyrkii samalla vauhdittamaan Ukrainan sotaa koskevaa diplomatiaa.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trumpin on määrä tavata Ukrainan presidentti Volodymyr Zelenskyi tällä viikolla Naton huippukokouksen yhteydessä Ankarassa. Valkoinen talo kertoi tapaamisesta 5. heinäkuuta, kun Washington pyrkii elvyttämään pysähtyneitä rauhanpyrkimyksiä Venäjän hyökkäyssodassa ja painostaa Eurooppaa kantamaan suuremman vastuun maanosan puolustuksesta.

## Puolustusmenot kokouksen keskiössä

Trumpin odotetaan nostavan Ankarassa esiin vaatimuksensa siitä, että liittolaismaat kasvattaisivat puolustusmenonsa viiteen prosenttiin bruttokansantuotteesta seuraavan vuosikymmenen aikana. Yhdysvaltain Nato-suurlähettiläs Matt Whitaker sanoi ennen kokousta, että Trump odottaa kaikkien liittolaisten etenevän nopeasti kohti viiden prosentin tavoitetta.

Naton pääsihteeri Mark Rutte on jo aiemmin korostanut liittolaisten kasvaneita menolupauksia. Oval Officen tapaamisessa viime kuussa hän esitteli Trumpille laskelmia, joiden mukaan liittolaiset ovat lisänneet sitoumuksiaan vuodesta 2017 lähtien. Washingtonissa toimiva Hudson-instituutin tutkija Luke Coffey kuvasi Ankaran kokousta eräänlaiseksi ensimmäiseksi väliarvioksi viime vuoden Haagin huippukokouksen jälkeen.

Puolustusmenokeskustelu käydään samalla, kun Trumpilla on ollut jännitteitä useiden liittolaisten kanssa muun muassa Iranin sodan ja Grönlantia koskevien puheidensa vuoksi.

## Ukraina hakee tukea diplomatialle

Trumpin ja Zelenskyin tapaamisesta ilmoitettiin päivä sen jälkeen, kun Trump oli puhunut erikseen puhelimessa sekä Zelenskyin että Venäjän presidentin Vladimir Putinin kanssa. Zelenskyin mukaan hän kertoi Trumpille rintamatilanteesta, ja johtajat sopivat jatkavansa keskusteluja Naton huippukokouksessa.

Zelenskyi kirjoitti X:ssä, että sodan lopettamiseen on todellinen mahdollisuus ja että Yhdysvaltain päättäväisyys on ratkaisevaa. Hän myös varoitti Ukrainan tiedustelutietojen viittaavan siihen, että Venäjä valmistelisi uutta laajaa ilmaiskukampanjaa Ukrainaa vastaan heinäkuun alun tappavien iskujen jälkeen.

Kremlin mukaan Trumpin noin puolentoista tunnin puhelussa Putinin kanssa Trump toisti valmiutensa jatkaa välityspyrkimyksiä. Putin puolestaan esitti jälleen Moskovan kannan, jonka mukaan mahdollisessa ratkaisussa on otettava huomioon Venäjän omat lähtökohdat konfliktin päättämiselle.
summary_bullets: Trumpin ja Zelenskyin on määrä tavata Naton huippukokouksen yhteydessä Ankarassa.
Yhdysvallat painostaa Nato-liittolaisia nostamaan puolustusmenojaan kohti viittä prosenttia BKT:stä.
Zelenskyi varoittaa Venäjän mahdollisesti valmistelevan uutta laajaa ilmaiskukampanjaa Ukrainaa vastaan.

Luke Coffey, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute, a conservative think thank in Washington, described the Ankara gathering as the "first report card" after last year's summit in The Hague.

"There is a real prospect to put an end to this war, and America's resolve is decisive," Zelenskyy wrote on X. Zelenskyy also warned that intelligence suggests Russia is preparing yet another massive air campaign against Ukraine, following the deadly barrage on the night of July 1–2. "This is in the spirit of Putin -- right after America's Independence Day and before the NATO summit in Ankara. Russia wants to add to the evil and kill people," Zelenskyy said in his video statement on July 5. The Kremlin said Trump's roughly 90-minute conversation with Putin included Trump's reiteration of his readiness to continue mediation efforts, while Putin repeated Moscow's position that any settlement must take account of Russia's "fundamental approach" to resolving the conflict.

The speed with which most NATO countries have tried to heed Trump's call to spend 5% of their annual gross domestic product on defense over the next decade underscores how the U.S. president has reshaped the alliance and bent it to his will — even as he continues to spar with its members over the Iran war, his flirtation with annexing Greenland, and various personal tiffs. "President Trump fully expects that all allies will step up immediately and get on the path to 5% and do it with urgency," Matt Whitaker, the U.S. ambassador to NATO, told reporters in a preview of the administration's message before this week's summit in Ankara.
